people.name: Marcus Bell
lines: Walk the Library gallery rounds with me after dusk — each reading room still keeps its order.
Capitol dome on the west, Library dome on the east, and four fanning walks down to the brick rows.

people.name: Nora
lines: Upper Senate Park leads north to Union Station; Pennsylvania Avenue runs west to the Mall.

people.name: Dev
lines: Even the stone fountains between the Capitol and the Library still hold rainwater.

signs.text: United States Capitol — marble steps silent under the white dome.
Library of Congress — bronze doors open for Marcus Bell's night rounds.
Capitol Forecourt — four fanning avenues descending into the brick rowhouses.
Constitution Terrace — stone walk linking the Capitol and Library.
Capitol Bookbinder — stitched folios shelved dry behind brick walls.
Seward Tea Parlor — shuttered bay window overlooking the fanning plaza.
East Capitol Watch — brass bell hung beside the terrace stair.
Pennsylvania Row — brick rowhouses facing the west Capitol lawn.
Hillside Apothecary — mortar and brass scales kept behind the counter.
Capitol Clock Repair — pendulum chimes faint beneath the porch.
East Alley Garden — walled courtyard facing the Library wing.
Terrace Reflecting Pool — rainwater mirroring both white domes.
West Capitol Steps — descending toward Pennsylvania Avenue and the Mall.
Upper Senate Park Gate — avenue north toward Union Station.
Pennsylvania Avenue Gate — broad road west toward the National Mall.
Supreme Court Steps — marble portico rising east of the Library.
West Capitol Pond — quiet lily basin beside the fanning walks.
Seward Square South — brick rowhouse crossroad beneath tall elms.
East Capitol Street — double row of Victorian bays stretching east.
Independence Avenue Row — iron fences bordering the south Capitol blocks.
South Rowhouse Court — mossy cobblestones behind the carriage houses.
Lower Hill Alley — shuttered brick basements swept clear of rubble.
Marion Park Garden — wrought-iron gate facing the lower avenues.
North Terrace Gate — stone steps climbing back toward the Senate park.
Southwest Fanning Walk — diagonal gravel path framing the west lawn.
Southeast Fanning Walk — diagonal path descending toward East Capitol.
Capitol Boundary Stone — carved mile marker half-covered in ivy.
East Garden Steps — brick walk descending behind the Supreme Court.
Library North Annex — carved stone lintels facing the Senate lawns.
